Inputs: lease.granted and lease.expired, seat.heartbeat, the tick:stall entity
Mechanism: heartbeat age against the bound, kill, revoke
A long-lived seat parked on an interactive prompt
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
Retries: three attempts, then recover and report
Many agents at once: the collision answer
State paths written and the cleanup script for each

pointers.shared: Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.sentence: On every stall tick the Go service compares the age of each live run's last heartbeat with the run's stall bound and its deadline, and for every run past either it kills the process, revokes the lease with a new fencing token and writes one stall record, so no run can hold a slot or a ticket for ever and no agent is asked whether it is stuck.
purpose.is: The replacement for the one-minute idle alarm, the Haiku monitor and the compliance officer (D17, C49; K04): a seat is a one-shot run that ends at its output, so idle cannot exist; a run with no event for the stall bound is killed and retried by N-11 (Symphony SPEC.md lines 823 to 829).
A probe, never an opinion (V08): the only inputs are timestamps in the store and the process table; no model reads a pane.

Also the one-minute detector for a long-lived seat (the architect, the orchestrator) parked on a blocking interactive prompt: owner order 2026-10-13 02:01Z, no agent sits idle for more than one minute; the 2026-10-14 incident is in section prompt-parked. Still a probe: herdr's own agent status event plus the transcript age, never a model and never pane text.
purpose.is-not: Not a liveness judge of system processes: units are supervised by systemd and reported by N-06's health; this node judges seat runs and code-role runs that hold a lease.
Not a retry: the stall record is a failure record for N-11, which decides attempt n plus 1 or dead.
purpose.decisions: D02 (C36), D08 (C46), D17 (C49), V08, T06 (lease with heartbeat, generation and compare-and-swap; never stolen when liveness is unknown), T07 rejected below.

field.name: key, holder, token, generation, expires_at, heartbeat_seconds

record.field: A lease with a holder is a live run; expires_at moves on every renewal (N-02 lease.renewed) that the launcher's heartbeat makes.

N-02's sweep found a lease past expires_at with no renewal, freed the key and bumped the generation; N-02 names N-12 as the reader that kills the run. It is the lease side of a dead launcher (reason lease-expired below).

field.name: run_id, ticket, lease (key, token, generation), renewed

record.field: The run heartbeating and whether this heartbeat renewed the lease at N-02; a renewal refused (token stale, generation moved) is the launcher's own signal to end the run (N-15 output).

UTC second the launcher wrote it, every lease.heartbeat_seconds (default 30, shared/state-store.xml#config-keys; Optio renews every 20 s with a 60 s lease, I03 section 6). The lease ttl N-02 sets (900 s) is far longer on purpose, so a short service restart never expires a live run's lease; a dead launcher is found by this node's 3-beat bound (90 s), not by the ttl. The store keeps the latest heartbeat per run_id (upsert, table heartbeats).

The mtime of the run's session transcript, which moves on every model turn and tool call; the stall signal this node compares with the role's stall bound (N-15: the stall timer compares progress_at with stall_seconds).
The process the launcher supervises and when it started, for the kill and the pid-reuse guard.
Counters, so the Machine screen shows motion; this node branches on ages only.

Default 15 (config stall.tick_seconds, N-06 schedule); the bound minus the interval is the longest a stall stays unseen (SPEC-16.F f-stall-visible: poll interval plus the smallest deadline must not pass the visible-within bound; refused at start otherwise). An entity broadcast in process, not a log record (N-06).

field.name: pane_id, seat, session_id, status, message, at

record.field: herdr's pane.agent_status_changed event for a registered long-lived seat, raised when the harness Notification hook reports blocked (rebuild/investigation/L04-herdr.md#7-decisions-an-llm-makes-that-a-rule-could-make, the hooks map); message is the harness notification text, matched by code against the prompt rules and never read from the pane. Consumed only by section prompt-parked.

input.reads: The dispatch record of each live lease (deadline, role); the roles table (stall_seconds per role); the halt record; the registered long-lived seats and their newest transcript mtime.

record.field: lease key, colon, generation at kill time; one per revoked generation, ever.

field.name: ticket, phase, attempt, dispatch_id, run_id, lease_key, old_token, new_generation

record.field: The run killed and the lease revoked.

no-progress (now minus progress_at above the role's stall bound while heartbeats still arrive: the model is stuck), launcher-dead (the newest heartbeat older than 3 x heartbeat_seconds: the launcher process stopped writing), deadline (the dispatch deadline passed with progress still arriving), no-first-heartbeat (no heartbeat within start.grace_seconds of the dispatch, default 120: the run never started; replaces wake confirmation), lease-expired (N-02's lease.expired arrived, the lease side of launcher-dead).
killed is true when the process was ended by this node, false when it was already gone.
1 to 3, how many signals were needed.
A process that survived SIGTERM and SIGKILL three times; a system-lane fault.
seat, colon, session id, colon, the UTC second the blocked status began; one per parked episode, re-carded under the same key (recard_count) rather than duplicated.

field.name: seat, pane_id, session_id, rule, action, blocked_since, detected_at, age_seconds, recard_count

record.field: The seat parked, the rule that matched (or unmatched), the action chosen (card, answer, down) and how long it had been parked when detected.
Closes the episode of a prompt.parked; N-28 marks the card done.

output.ends-when: Every live lease past a bound has a stall record and a revoked lease; a lease within bounds ends the traversal with no record; the next stall tick is a new traversal.

mechanism.where: Go package stall inside the service; Judge(leases, heartbeats, dispatches, roles, now) is pure and returns kill intents; the engine kills, revokes and writes.
mechanism.step: One read transaction: every lease with a holder; the newest seat.heartbeat per run_id (table heartbeats); unhandled lease.expired records; the dispatch per lease; the roles table.

For each lease: progress age equals now minus the newest heartbeat's progress_at; launcher age equals now minus the newest heartbeat's at; both equal now minus the dispatch's at when no heartbeat exists. Bound equals the role's stall_seconds (defaults: worker 300, reviewer 300, spec-author 300, gate 60; Symphony stall_timeout_ms 300000; SPEC-16.F f-stall-deadline: deadlines are per kind because a suite and a merge take different times; the validator is code inside the service with its own bounds, N-18, and holds no seat lease). Launcher bound equals 3 x lease.heartbeat_seconds (90 s at the default 30, shared/state-store.xml#config-keys). First-heartbeat grace equals start.grace_seconds (default 120) when no heartbeat exists.

Stalled when progress age is above the bound (no-progress), or launcher age is above the launcher bound (launcher-dead), or no heartbeat exists and the age is above the grace (no-first-heartbeat), or now is past the dispatch deadline (deadline), or a lease.expired names the key (lease-expired). Not stalled otherwise; end for this lease. A clock skew guard: a heartbeat with at or progress_at in the future by more than stall.tick_seconds is counted as now (the store's clock is N-06's; the launcher's is the same host, D22).

If the snapshot read failed (step 1 timed out), liveness is unknown and nothing is revoked this tick (T06: never stolen when liveness is unknown; S04 section 8 item 7: alive when unknown). The tick is counted; three unknown ticks in a row write store.unreachable 500 once.

Revoke first, kill second: compare-and-swap the lease's generation from the snapshot value to plus 1, holder to empty, token to the next store-wide token (N-02 revoke verb). Refused: the lease changed under us (a heartbeat renewed it in the window, or N-02's sweep already expired it); re-read and re-judge once; if still stalled, retry the swap; otherwise end. For lease-expired the swap is already done by N-02 and this step only confirms the generation. After the swap every write with the old token is refused by N-01 as stale (N-02 lease_stale), so the run is fenced before it is killed.

Kill the process named in the newest heartbeat's pid (or the dispatch's claimed pid from N-15 when no heartbeat exists): SIGTERM, wait 2 s, SIGKILL, wait 2 s, up to 3 rounds (herdr/bin/seat-lib.sh lines 300 to 311: 3 tries x 2 s). A pid that is gone before the first signal is killed false. The launcher (N-15) sees the kill and writes seat.result blocked with terminal_reason killed_stall (or killed_deadline, killed_lease_lost, matching the reason); if it cannot (the launcher itself died), the stall record stands alone and N-11 handles it.

Write the stall record keyed by the lease key and the new generation. N-11 reads it as a failure of the attempt (and marks the launcher's echo handled by the same attempt); N-41 shows it; N-14 releases the workspace on the stall record (its own volume).
mechanism.invariant: A run is fenced before it is killed, and killed before its stall is retried: order revoke, kill, record, so a zombie can never post a result after the retry started (fencing token).
One stall record per lease generation; a late heartbeat after revoke is a 409 at N-01, logged, never a resurrection.
mechanism.diagram: flowchart TD T["tick:stall entity"] --> S{"snapshot ok?"} S -- no --> U["liveness unknown: revoke nothing, count"] S -- yes --> J{"per lease: progress age above bound, launcher age above 3 x heartbeat, no first heartbeat past grace, past deadline, or lease.expired?"} J -- no --> E["end, next tick"] J -- yes --> R{"CAS lease: generation+1, token+1, holder empty"} R -- refused --> RJ["re-read, re-judge once"] RJ -- "still stalled" --> R RJ -- "renewed" --> E R -- ok --> K["SIGTERM 2 s, SIGKILL 2 s, up to 3 rounds"] K -- gone --> W["stall 500 (lease key:generation)"] K -- survives x3 --> KF["stall.kill.failed 500 to N-28"] W --> N11["N-11 attempt n+1 or dead"] W --> N41["N-41 alerts"]

prompt-parked.what-broke: 2026-10-14 06:46Z to 08:46Z: the architect, a long-lived interactive seat, sat two hours on a blocking model-limit choice prompt. It held no launcher lease, so no heartbeat or stall bound applied to it, the retired idle alarm no longer existed, and nothing noticed until the owner did. The owner rule is that no agent sits idle for more than one minute (2026-10-13 02:01Z). The prompt was cleared at 08:46Z by switching the seat to Opus 5.5, the architect's ruled model (roles/architect.json, model.claude); that answer needed no owner decision and is the precedent for rule pp-model-limit.
prompt-parked.why-it-mattered: The whole line is ruled through the architect; one parked prompt stopped every ruling, every card answer routed to the architect lane and every spec-author cut for two hours with all lamps green.
prompt-parked.rule: A seat registered as long-lived in scheduler/config/seats.json (the architect and the orchestrator) is parked when herdr reports its agent status blocked (event pane.agent_status_changed, fed by the harness Notification hook) and the newest transcript mtime is older than stall.prompt_park_seconds (default 30). The status event starts the clock; the stall tick (15 s) judges it. Worst case from the prompt appearing to the prompt.parked record is 30 s + 15 s = 45 s, and N-28 posts the card inside the next 15 s, so the whole path is under one minute (config check: stall.prompt_park_seconds + stall.tick_seconds + 15 stays at or below 60).

The probe reads a status field herdr computes and the harness notification message; it sends no keystroke and reads no pane text. A blocked status with a moving transcript is not parked (the harness is working through the prompt). herdr unreachable is liveness unknown and nothing is written, the same T06 rule as step m-unknown; three unknown ticks write store.unreachable 500 once.

Routing is a table, scheduler/config/prompt-rules.json (the planned home; this volume describes the rule entry and the file is a build-ticket output, never written by the design), matched in order by regex over the notification message. Each entry names an id, a match regex, an action (answer, card or down), and for an answer the standing answer and the policy that owns it. Three classes: model-limit (a model or usage limit choice) routes to action answer by rule pp-model-limit and to card only when the seat's role has no ruled model; permission and trust prompts route to action answer only when the entry names an owner-ruled standing answer for that prompt class (a standing policy with a deadline and a default, V17), else card; an unmatched message routes to card. An answer is sent by N-42 control.action, never by this node. A one-shot run that blocks is not routed here: it is a stall and N-11 retries it.

Owner ruling, architect, 2026-10-14 ~09:10Z: a model-limit prompt on a seat is not routed to an owner card; a standing rule answers it. The entry of prompt-rules.json is id model-limit, action answer, answer switch-model, with these fields: match (regex over the harness notification message for a model or usage limit choice); role (taken from the seat's registration in scheduler/config/seats.json); model (read at answer time from the role file, roles/ROLE.json key model, entry for the seat's runtime, for example roles/architect.json model.claude, which is claude-opus-5-5, an Opus by owner rule; workers, reviewers, testers, mergers and the orchestrator carry Sonnet; the spec-author file names its own class and the file, not this volume, is the authority); never_option (any option that spends extra credits, usage beyond the plan, an overage or a pay-as-you-go top-up; such an option is never selected whatever the prompt lists); fallback card, taken only when the role has no ruled model for the runtime, when the ruled model is not among the prompt's options, or when the only way forward spends extra credits. Mechanics: N-12 matches the message, resolves the model from the role file, writes prompt.parked 423 with rule model-limit, action answer and answer_model set; N-42 sends the switch to that model by control.action (the harness model command, never a keystroke typed at a menu by this node); the park clears when the status leaves blocked, and prompt.cleared 200 closes the episode. If the same episode is still blocked one stall.prompt_recard_seconds (900) after the answer, the answer failed and the entry falls through to a card under the same key. The 2026-10-14 incident (architect parked 06:46Z to 08:46Z, answered by switching to Opus 5.5) is the precedent. The cost the rule accepts: the seat may run on a model the owner would not have picked that hour, so the choice is bounded to the role's ruled model and never to a larger spend; a spend decision still belongs to the owner and still goes to a card.

action card (a prompt class with no standing answer, a role with no ruled model, an unmatched message, or an answer that failed) writes prompt.parked 423 and N-28 posts one card to the owner naming the seat, how long it has been parked and the prompt message, with the options the rule lists. The card is re-posted under the same key every stall.prompt_recard_seconds (default 900) while the status stays blocked, so a missed card cannot become a silent stall; the park clears when the status leaves blocked or the transcript moves, and a prompt.cleared 200 record closes the episode.

wait.on: a registered long-lived seat leaving blocked
wait.timeout: stall.prompt_park_seconds 30 to the record, then recard every stall.prompt_recard_seconds 900
wait.fallback: this node's own verdict: prompt.parked 423 and a card; if N-28 fails to post, stall.write.failed 500 as for any record write

prompt-parked.many-agents: Several long-lived seats may be parked at once: one idempotency key per seat and episode, so a second stall goroutine's write is a 409; the status event and the tick may race, and the compare-and-swap on the episode entity (prompt:SEAT) lets one writer open it and one clear it, the loser re-reads and ends.
prompt-parked.never: No nudge, no keystroke, no Escape, no pane read, no model asked what the prompt says; the architect is never woken to answer its own prompt; no standing answer ever picks an option that spends extra credits, and no model-limit prompt goes to the owner while the role has a ruled model.

start.sentence: Nothing here starts by an agent typing.
start.by: N-06 broadcasts the tick:stall entity every stall.tick_seconds (15) from the service's clock; each tick is a traversal.
start.restart: After a crash the first stall tick re-reads leases and heartbeats from the store; a run that died with the service has no fresh heartbeat and is judged by age like any other; a run that survived (the launcher is its own process) keeps heartbeating and is left alone.
start.never: No patrol script, no compliance officer, no monitor seat, no pane read (K04, K06); the prompt probe of section prompt-parked reads herdr's status event and the harness notification message, not pane text.

wait.on: N-01 read of leases and heartbeats
wait.fallback: liveness unknown: revoke nothing; three in a row write store.unreachable 500 once; the bound keeps growing, so a real stall is caught on the first good tick
retry 1 s, 2 s, 4 s; then the lease is left as is and the next tick re-judges; stall.write.failed 500 once per lease key after the third tick
next round, up to 3; then stall.kill.failed 500 to N-28 (a process the kernel will not end is a host fault for the owner)

wait.on: the next heartbeat of a run
wait.timeout: 3 x heartbeat_seconds (launcher), or start.grace_seconds before the first
wait.fallback: this node's own verdict: stall launcher-dead or no-first-heartbeat
this node's own verdict: stall no-progress

wait.on: the run ending by its dispatch deadline
wait.timeout: the deadline (worker 3600 s default; Symphony turn_timeout_ms)
wait.fallback: stall reason deadline even while heartbeats arrive, so a run that is busy for ever still ends

waits.rule: Timers are context deadlines and the fake clock in tests; no time.Sleep outside the kill rounds, which are bounded at 12 s total and run in their own goroutine so the 15 s tick never waits on a kill.

step.name: kill
step.then: stall.kill.failed 500 to N-28 and N-41; the lease stays revoked so the ticket moves on; the process is the owner's to end

retries.not-retried: A stall is never retried by this node; N-11 owns the next attempt. A kill is never repeated after a stall record is written for that generation.
retries.report: Every then clause is a record; a kill that fails is one card, never a loop of signals.

many-agents.readers: Any number of seats run at once, each with its own lease and heartbeat stream; this node judges each lease on its own row, so N seats cost N rows per tick and no lock.
many-agents.two-timers: Two stall goroutines (a restart overlap, or two service processes before the leader lease node:N-07:leader settles) may both judge one lease stalled; the compare-and-swap on generation lets exactly one revoke; the loser re-reads, sees the new generation, and ends. N-02's sweep (lease.expired) is a third writer on the same row and the same swap settles it. The kill is idempotent (a gone pid is killed false) and the stall record key lease key:generation makes a second write a 409.
many-agents.heartbeat-versus-revoke: A heartbeat and a revoke race on one lease: N-01 serialises writes on the lease row; a heartbeat that commits first renews expires_at and the revoke's compare-and-swap is refused (re-judge once: if progress_at still shows no progress the swap is retried, because a live launcher with a stuck model is exactly no-progress; if progress moved, it ends); a revoke that commits first makes the heartbeat's renewal a lease_stale 409, which the launcher reads as its signal to end (N-15 output).
many-agents.stale-result: A killed run's late seat.result carries the old token and is refused by N-01; the fresh seat of attempt n plus 1 carries the new token; two results for one attempt cannot both land (T06; S04 section 8 item 7).
many-agents.pid-reuse: A pid reused by another process between the heartbeat and the kill is guarded by started_at in the heartbeat: the kill checks the process start time in the process table against it and skips a mismatch, writing killed false with kill_reason pid-reused.
many-agents.conflict-reports: Every refused compare-and-swap and every 409 is logged with the key and counted; never a silent overwrite.
many-agents.test: Test case two-timers-one-lease: two Judge plus revoke rounds over one stalled lease write one stall record and one 409 (checklist c-two-timers); test heartbeat-wins: a heartbeat committed between snapshot and swap leaves the run alive.

emits.acts: N-11 attempt n plus 1 or dead; N-41 alerts; N-14 releases the workspace
N-28 marks the card done; N-41 clears the alert

N-42 sends the standing answer where prompt-rules.json names one (model-limit: switch the seat to its role's ruled model, never an extra-credit option); N-28 one card to the owner only where no standing answer applies (re-carded every 900 s while parked); N-41 alerts

meets.kinds: stale-token on heartbeat, lease CAS refused
meets.acts: logged and counted; the collision answer

reads.acts: under halt this node still judges and revokes: a halt stops new work, not the bound on running work; the owner's USERHALT interrupts seats through N-42's control.action, which ends runs by their launchers, and this node records nothing for a run that ended cleanly

state-paths.root: $COQ_STATE as in ../N-07/spec.xml#state-paths; path elements in N-45's generator form.
state-paths.path: Rows: stall and stall.kill.failed records; the leases table fields generation, token and holder by compare-and-swap. Heartbeats are an upsert per run_id (N-15), so they do not grow; terminal runs' heartbeat rows prune with the run after retention (N-01's row).
One line per judged lease with ages and bound; rotated daily.
state-paths.never: No pid file of its own (the launcher's pid is in the heartbeat), no pane, no file under the repository.

out.note: not drawn in dag.md; owner-acts kinds reach N-28 by the status code map

side-effect.what: the run's process is killed; the launcher writes seat.result blocked with terminal_reason killed_stall, killed_deadline or killed_lease_lost
the workspace is released on the stall record

schema.defs: stall, stall_kill_failed; seat.heartbeat, lease_granted, lease_expired and tick are references to the N-15, N-02 and N-06 schemas; base as in N-07.

permissions.process: The Go service user unit; it runs as the same user as the launchers so it may signal their processes (D22: service and seats on the WSL host).
permissions.reads: leases, heartbeats, dispatches, roles table, halt record; the process table for pid and start time.
permissions.writes: stall, stall.kill.failed, stall.write.failed, store.unreachable records; the lease row by compare-and-swap (generation, token, holder); the stall log; SIGTERM and SIGKILL to run processes named by heartbeats.
permissions.never: No signal to a process not named by a heartbeat or a dispatch claim; no herdr call except the agent-status subscription of section prompt-parked; no pane text; no keystroke; no prompt; no edit of heartbeat or dispatch records.
permissions.seat: No seat can write a stall or revoke a lease (N-01 writer identity); a seat's only liveness duty is to keep producing events, which the launcher turns into heartbeats; the seat never writes a heartbeat itself (a self-report is an opinion, V08).

counter.name: stall_total
counter.from: stall records, by reason and role

gauge.name: progress_age_max_seconds
gauge.from: the oldest progress_at age among live runs

gauge.name: heartbeat_age_max_seconds
gauge.from: the oldest heartbeat age among live runs

gauge.name: runs_near_bound
gauge.from: live runs with progress age above half their bound

lamp.name: stall
lamp.green: no live run past half its progress bound
lamp.amber: a run past half its bound
lamp.red: a stall in the last tick, or store unreachable

alert.to: N-41 at once; the card is N-11's at dead

runbook.bring-up: N-15 writing seat.heartbeat; roles table with stall_seconds per role; set stall.enabled true (shadow first: judge and log, no revoke, for one day; then live). Proof: a stall record no-progress for a test run whose model process was paused with SIGSTOP for longer than its bound while the launcher kept heartbeating, a stall launcher-dead for a run whose launcher was paused, and each run's late result refused as a 409.
runbook.read-status: Scheduler.Status lists live runs with heartbeat age, bound and deadline; the Machine screen shows one run; the Alerts screen shows stalls.
runbook.raise-a-bound: Edit the role's stall_seconds in the roles table through a ticket; Scheduler.Reload; the config check keeps the visible bound.
runbook.kill-failed: The card names the pid; the owner ends it on the host (one time); the ticket already moved on because the lease was revoked.
runbook.recover-store-unreachable: N-01 runbook; this node revokes nothing until the store answers.
runbook.registry: Generated into shared/cleanup-registry.json from the state-paths element (../N-45/spec.xml#state-paths); heartbeat rows prune with N-01's store row.
